Additional comments:
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my traineeship host

questions.question: How easy was it to find housing? *
questions.answer: I got help from the contract person at the receiving university. They knew the town better (of course) and helped out a great deal with the initial communication, since germans prefer speaking German.

questions.question: Additional comments:
How relevant did you find your traineeship for your future employment prospects? *
questions.answer:
Very relevant. It was very nice to visit another laboratory and see how the structure was similar or different. This for me was one of the main points.
For future employment, I can't really tell yet since I am still a master student. But I could expect future employers to look positively on my exchange in another laboratory.

questions.question: How relevant did you find your traineeship for your academic programme at UCPH *
questions.answer: Very academic. Most of the techniques are similar, with slight differences. This was interesting to learn, and also helped me better understand and develop academic interests and understandings.

questions.question: Additional comments
questions.answer: No

questions.question: How well did the academic level at UCPH coincide with the tasks completed during your traineeship? *
questions.answer: Very nice! It is the same academic level. Although at the institute there are more post docs and PhD students presents than backhome. So I had a lot more discussions and more views on things than I would otherwise have back home.

questions.question: Please elaborate *
questions.answer: It was very nice :)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The need to pay deposit for various keys to both the laboratory and the housing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less than expected. The travel was although more expensive in germany - not the Deutschland ticket which costs 58 euro per month. But the expensive part is the travel to Bochum from Copenhagen and vice versa. Going by train the DB is very expensive, compared to a FlixBus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your traineeship destination (city/region)? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some great friends here in Bochum already, so they showed me around the sites, took care of me and showed me everything great about germany!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available at your traineeship destination (organization/city/region)? *
questions.answer:
We went to see Dortmund play in the bundesliga, and luckily my friend had free tickets for us. 
There were a lot of planned holidays in germany during my traineeship, so a lot of the days off were used with friends to enjoy the city.

questions.question: Which non-academic activities would you recommend to future trainees visiting the same destination (organization/city/region)? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely go see football, it is a huge cultural thing in Bochum / Ruhr area!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting trainees see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the botanical garden, around the city, Dusseldorf or enjoy German company!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your trainee host? *
questions.answer: Very Easy. However, the mast majority of germans are somewhat poor in English - outside of academia and university. I have many examples of people asking me for help, but since I couldn't speak German and they spoke poor English they decided to not speak with me.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of the destination (city/country)? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - Bochum - Germany.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with locals? *
questions.answer: Speak with them, they are very keen on talking! even tho their English might not be perfect. The academic vibe in Bochum is high, it's quite different from Copenhagen, since Bochum is one big university town.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barriers

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Kindness and the help I got from friends, colleagues and others.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going on a traineeship to the same city/region? *
questions.answer:
1. Get some sort of support network so show you around town.
2. Get situated in the city, learn about the public transport system in the region.
3. Maybe learn a little German before going, so you can understand basic conversations. No need to speak, but it is nice to know a little bit.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future traineeship students? *
questions.answer: No I think I listed it all.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your traineeship experience? *
questions.answer: The experienced gained, I mean here I n Bochum there are a lot more of scientists, and they are very very good. I was taught some amazing ways to perform the techniques I do back home, and I got them fine tuned here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the traineeship? *
questions.answer: The time frame. I wished I had more time here, but I also do have friends, family and relationship backhome that I need to take care of. I wished I could stay here for longer.

questions.question: Is there anything UCPH could have done different (before/during/after) in regard to the traineeship experience? *
questions.answer: No, it was perfect!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
